hook.situation: After class, a friend asks what the teacher said. You need to pass along a statement, a question, and an instruction without mixing the endings.
objectives: Report statements with -다고 했어요 and recognize the spoken contraction -대요.
Use -는지 when a question is embedded inside 알다, 모르다, 확인하다, or 궁금하다.
hook.whyItMatters: Reported speech is not one pattern. Korean changes the ending depending on what the original sentence was: a statement, a question, or an instruction.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-다고 했어요 — reported statement
grammarNotes.mentalModel: First ask: was the original sentence a statement? If yes, use -다고 했어요 or the shorter spoken -대요.
grammarNotes.formation: Present action verbs take -ㄴ다고/-는다고: 간다고, 먹는다고. Adjectives take -다고: 바쁘다고. Past uses -았/었다고. Nouns use -(이)라고.

examples.en: The teacher said the exam is on Friday.
examples.note: A statement is being passed along respectfully.

examples.en: My friend said they are busy today.
They say they are coming tomorrow.
examples.note: -대요 is the common spoken contraction of -다고 해요.

exceptions: A reported instruction uses -(으)라고 하다: 숙제를 제출하라고 하셨어요.
Do not copy English tense backshift. Keep the Korean content in the form that matches the original meaning.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-냐고 물어봤어요 — reported question
grammarNotes.mentalModel: If the original sentence was a question, mark it as a question inside the report with -냐고.
grammarNotes.formation: Attach -냐고 to the verb or adjective stem in common speech: 오냐고, 바쁘냐고. Past uses -았/었냐고. Nouns use -(이)냐고.

examples.en: My friend asked what time we are meeting.
examples.note: The original was a question: 몇 시에 만나요?

examples.en: They asked whether I submitted the homework.
They asked when the exam is.

exceptions: Do not use -다고 just because the whole English sentence now says 'asked that/if'. Korean keeps the inner sentence marked as a question.
묻다 is the dictionary verb, but 물어보다 is the natural everyday choice in many conversations.

grammarNotes.title: V-는지 / A-(으)ㄴ지 / N인지 — embedded question
grammarNotes.mentalModel: -는지 turns a question into a chunk that another verb can use: know, not know, check, wonder, ask.
grammarNotes.formation: Action verbs take -는지, adjectives take -(으)ㄴ지, nouns with 이다 become N인지. Future/uncertain meaning uses -(으)ㄹ지.

examples.en: Do you know when the exam is?
Please check what time we are meeting.
I am not sure whether I submitted the homework.

exceptions: -는지 does not automatically mean someone asked the question. It is an embedded question.
If you are reporting that someone asked, use -냐고 물어봤어요.

exampleSentence.en: The teacher said we will take it on Friday.
My friend asked what time we are meeting.
Do you know when the exam is?
The teacher told us to submit the homework.
The teacher says the exam is on Friday.

extendedVocabulary.english: to ask; to ask and find out

exampleSentence.en: I asked my friend when the exam is.

exampleSentence.ko: 잘 못 들었으면 다시 말해 달라고 해요.
exampleSentence.en: If you did not hear it well, ask them to say it again.
exampleSentence.note: Useful repair phrase when reported information is unclear.

exampleSentence.en: They told us to submit the homework by tomorrow.
Do you know when the exam is?
They asked whether I submitted the homework.
exampleSentence.note: A practical school/work verb for reported questions.

exampleSentence.en: Please check what time we are meeting.
I will pass the details on to my friend.
exampleSentence.note: The communication job of reported speech.

readingText.title: 선생님이 뭐라고 하셨어요?
readingText.body: 수업이 끝난 뒤 친구에게 내용을 전할 때는 원래 문장이 어떤 종류였는지 먼저 봐야 해요. 선생님이 '금요일에 시험을 봐요'라고 말한 내용은 '금요일에 본다고 하셨어요'로 전할 수 있어요. 질문을 전할 때는 '-냐고'를 써요. 그래서 '몇 시에 만나요?'는 '몇 시에 만나냐고 물어봤어요'가 돼요. 하지만 누가 질문한 것이 아니라 내가 답을 알고 싶은 상황이면 '-는지'가 자연스러워요. '시험이 언제인지 알아요?'처럼 큰 문장 안에 질문을 넣는 거예요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: When passing along class information, first identify the original sentence type. Statements use -다고 했어요, questions use -냐고 물어봤어요, and embedded questions use -는지 inside verbs like know, not know, or check.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 원래 문장이 statement이면 어떤 표현을 써요?
질문을 전할 때는 어떤 표현을 써요?
큰 문장 안에 질문을 넣을 때는 어떤 표현을 써요?

culturalNote.title: The ending carries the original sentence type
culturalNote.body: In Korean, the listener can often tell whether the original was a statement, question, or instruction from the reported ending itself. That is why choosing -다고, -냐고, or -(으)라고 matters.
culturalNote.tip: Before reporting someone else's words, label the source sentence: statement, question, or instruction.

inlineExercises.prompt: The teacher said, '금요일에 시험을 봐요.' Which report is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: The original is a statement, so use -다고 하셨어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Your friend asked, '몇 시에 만나요?' Which report is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: The original is a question, so use -냐고 물어봤어요.
알다 takes the embedded question form -는지/-인지.

bullets: Embedded questions: -는지 with 알다, 모르다, 확인하다, 궁금하다.
